# markdown-regex

> Zero-dependency TypeScript RegExp constants for extracting headers, links, images, lists, and code from Markdown. Not a CommonMark parser.

- Repo: https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/markdown-regex
- README: https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex/blob/main/README.md
- Agent guide: https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- Full API: https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex/blob/main/llms-full.txt
- Source index: https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex/blob/main/src/index.ts
- extract(): https://github.com/LLazyEmail/markdown-regex/blob/main/src/extract.ts

## Use when

You need to pull ATX headers, inline links/images, lists, or code spans out of a string without standing up a parser.

## Do not use when

You need an AST, nested emphasis, setext headings, reference links, or CommonMark compliance. Use remark, micromark, or markdown-it.

## Install

```
npm install markdown-regex
```

GitHub is 2.1.x. npm `latest` may still be 1.2.0 (legacy JS, `REGEXP_EM`). Prefer git until 2.x is on `latest`:

```
npm install github:LLazyEmail/markdown-regex#main
```

## Public surface

Named exports only. Node 20+. ESM + CJS + IIFE (`MarkdownRegex`).

- Regexes: `REGEXP_HEADER`, `REGEXP_H2`, `REGEXP_H3`, `REGEXP_IMAGE`, `REGEXP_LINK`, `REGEXP_STRONG`, `REGEXP_ITALIC`, `REGEXP_DEL`, `REGEXP_CODE`, `REGEXP_INLINE_CODE`, `REGEXP_FENCED_CODE`, `REGEXP_HTML`, `REGEXP_Q`, `REGEXP_BLOCKQUOTE`, `REGEXP_HR`, `REGEXP_PARAGRAPH`, `REGEXP_BR`, `REGEXP_EMPTY_BLOCKQUOTE`, `REGEXP_UL_LIST`, `REGEXP_OL_LIST`, `REGEXP_EMPTY_UL`, `REGEXP_EMPTY_OL`
- Helper: `extract(markdown: string): ExtractResult`
- v1 rename: `REGEXP_EM` → `REGEXP_ITALIC`

Prefer `extract()` over running every regex on raw Markdown; it strips fenced and inline code first.
